subject: Singapore
note: Cited to pinned Wikipedia revisions (trusted_secondary): Geography of Singapore and Land reclamation in Singapore. The two pages use different baselines (582 km2 'in the 1960s' vs '22% since independence in 1965'), so a script should use one at a time and say which. Dropped: any 'a fifth' or percentage not on the pages. The page gives only two area figures, so there is no year-by-year series.

claims.text: Singapore's land area has expanded from approximately 582 square kilometres in the 1960s to around 745 square kilometres in the 2020s, through extensive land reclamation since British colonisation in 1819.
claims.note: Derivable: 745 - 582 = 163 km2, about 28%; the page does not state that percentage.

claims.text: As of 2026, Singapore has a total land area of approximately 744.3 square kilometres.
Singapore has increased its land mass by 22% since independence in 1965, with land continuously being set aside for future use.
claims.note: Different baseline from the 582 km2 claim; do not mix the two on screen.

claims.text: Reclamation used earth sourced from Singapore's own hills, the seabed and neighbouring countries.
In 1981 Singapore Changi Airport opened after the clearing of roughly 2 km2 of swampland and the introduction of over 52,000,000 m3 of land- and seafill.
In 1992 the Marina Centre and Marina South reclamation projects, commissioned in the late 1970s, were completed, encompassing 360 ha of waterfront development.

Due to a global shortage of the required type of sand (river and beach sand, not desert sand), Singapore has switched to polders for reclamation since 2016: an area is surrounded by a dyke and pumped dry.
Nine hundred hectares of land off Changi Bay was announced for reclamation works in 2022 by the Housing and Development Board for future needs.
